questions.stem: A student counts the double bond in H2C=O as two separate directions and predicts four domains around carbon. Locate the counting error and give the corrected domain count.
conditions: Introductory valence-bond model and VSEPR rules apply; assume ideal coordination geometry unless specified.

answer.summary: Error location: the student counted the C=O double bond as two separate spatial directions. The two electron pairs of the double bond are shared between the same pair of nuclei (C and O), so they occupy a single internuclear region and constitute only ONE electron domain. Corrected count: 2 (C-H bonds) + 1 (C=O bond) = 3 electron domains around carbon (trigonal planar, sp2).

reasoning_route.why_valid: The student incorrectly counted the C=O double bond as two separate spatial directions.
Both electron pairs of the double bond share the same internuclear axis and constitute only one domain.
Corrected count: 2 (C-H bonds) + 1 (C=O bond) = 3 electron domains around carbon (trigonal planar, sp2).
Three domains repel to 120° trigonal planar geometry, confirming the corrected count.

questions.stem: The benchmark supplies this table: BF3 has three bonding domains and no central lone pair; CH4 has four bonding domains and no central lone pair. Match each central atom to the introductory sp2 or sp3 model, and check that the number of hybrid-orbital directions agrees with the domain count.

answer.summary: BF3: three domains and three sp2 hybrids. CH4: four domains and four sp3 hybrids. For these centres use valence 2s/2p language rather than ambiguous 1s + 2p shorthand.
